title: omp²: the next architecture
takeaway: Shared complexity needs one owner; public pre-release implementation is not a stable release.

scenes.title: A separate pre-release
scenes.visual: 12.1.1: diagram separates public branch from released product. 12.1.2: add a third target-architecture card; use no terminal recreation. Persistent gradeBadge C, pre-release/design badge and dateStamp throughout. All factual labels link to evidence cards.

sentences.text: There is another omp taking shape: omp², a public Rust rewrite whose branch explicitly warns about pre-release breaking changes.
sentences.spoken: There is another O-M-P taking shape: O-M-P squared, a public Rust rewrite whose branch explicitly warns about pre-release breaking changes.

sentences.text: This is not the released omp used in this walkthrough; the public branch and its target architecture are different things.
sentences.spoken: This is not the released omp used in this walkthrough; the public branch and its target architecture are different things.

scenes.title: Saving the whole session

Persistent gradeBadge C, pre-release/design badge and dateStamp throughout. All factual labels link to evidence cards.

sentences.text: The creator’s diagnosis includes omp itself, not just competitors: message history, extension state, background jobs, configuration, and interface state accumulated separate owners.

scenes.title: Commitments, not release announcements
scenes.visual: 12.3.1: diagram reveals the five exact commitment headings. 12.3.2: each pillar shows component-specific author-reported status, not a single pillar-complete badge. Keep the individual statuses and their source chips readable. Persistent gradeBadge C, pre-release/design badge and dateStamp throughout.

sentences.text: The playbook names five commitments: one authoritative session, a trusted control plane, bounded work, explicit compatibility, and views are projections.
sentences.spoken: The playbook names five commitments: one authoritative session, a trusted control plane, bounded work, explicit compatibility, and views are projections.

sentences.text: Their common thread is ownership: shared responsibilities belong in the engine, rather than being rebuilt independently by every extension.
sentences.spoken: Their common thread is ownership: shared responsibilities belong in the engine, rather than being rebuilt independently by every extension.
